verdict.rationale: DBOS runs as a library inside your own application processes, backed by your own Postgres, so execution and workflow state live in your infrastructure. DBOS also offers a vendor-managed Conductor that monitors and controls workflows and recovers interrupted ones to healthy executors (it can alternatively be self-hosted). The evidence never states that code and workflow data stay inside your network when the DBOS-managed Conductor is used, and orchestration itself happens in the library and Postgres rather than in Conductor. missing for 10: documented data-residency guarantees for managed Conductor, an explanation of how executors connect to the managed control plane, and independent corroboration of the hybrid deployment model.
